That suggests the type of the annotated object literal is being treated as incompatible with the declared interface type `{TwoNumbers}`/`TwoNumbers`, likely because the object literal is getting a nullable type `(TwoNumbers|null)` too early or incorrectly during scope creation / declaration.

Most suspicious static spot is `TypedScopeCreator.AbstractScopeBuilder.getDeclaredType(...)`, because for `@const` it returns `rValue.getJSType()` whenever the RHS already has a known type. In this test, the RHS is a casted object literal `/** @type {TwoNumbers} */ ({...})`, so if that cast has already evaluated to `(TwoNumbers|null)`, then the variable declaration is considered explicitly typed as `(TwoNumbers|null)`, and `TypeCheck.visitVar` reports `"initializing variable"` against the declared variable type from JSDoc on the var. That matches the observed bad message.

I want to verify whether `getDeclaredType` is indeed returning the RHS cast type `(TwoNumbers|null)` for the const variable and thereby causing the wrong diagnostic site/order.
